summary.text: Tom McClintock is a Republican who worked as a journalist and policy analyst before serving in the California Assembly and State Senate for 22 years. He has represented Sierra Nevada-area districts in the U.S. House since 2009, serves on the Judiciary, Natural Resources and Budget committees, and chairs the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement. His official biography describes his record on federal spending and taxes as a focus of his work.

paragraphs.text: Born in 1956 in Bronxville, New York; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from UCLA in 1978.

Worked as a journalist and public policy analyst before holding office. According to Wikipedia, he was elected chair of the Ventura County Republican Party at age 23 and served as chief of staff to State Senator Ed Davis.
Served in the California State Assembly (1982 to 1992 and 1996 to 2000) and the California State Senate (2000 to 2008); his official biography says he served 22 years in the state legislature.

Was the Republican nominee for State Controller twice; his official biography says he narrowly missed election in 2002 by 23/100ths of one percent, and that he ran as a candidate for governor in the 2003 recall election.

Won election to the U.S. House on November 4, 2008, defeating Democrat Charlie Brown, and took office in 2009; he now represents the 5th District, which stretches from the Sacramento suburbs toward the Fresno area and includes Yosemite National Park.
Serves on the House Judiciary Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and sits on the Subcommittee on the Constitution and Limited Government.

Is a senior member of the House Natural Resources Committee; he chaired its Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries from 2011 to 2015 and its Subcommittee on Federal Lands from 2015 to 2018. He is also a member of the House Budget Committee.
His official biography says the National Taxpayers Union rated him the best vote for taxpayers in the House four times, most recently in 2020.
